headline: Nearly 3,000 dead in Venezuela twin earthquakes
summary: Twin 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude shocks hit the coastal La Guaira area, leaving thousands homeless and an estimated 50,000 people missing.
details: Venezuela's devastating twin earthquakes, consisting of 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude shocks that occurred just 38 seconds apart, have killed 2,954 people according to official figures.
The disaster hit hardest in the coastal La Guaira area north of the capital Caracas, where numerous residential complexes were flattened and the Maiquetia international airport was damaged.
The United Nations estimates that as many as 50,000 people remain unaccounted for, while over 16,000 others have been injured.
International rescue teams, including squads from the US and South America, are now winding down search operations as the critical 72-hour window for survivors has passed.
The UN also estimates that the earthquakes caused $6.7 billion in physical damage, equivalent to approximately six percent of Venezuela's GDP.
Many Venezuelans have expressed anger over the government's slow response, claiming families had to dig out loved ones themselves before international aid arrived.
Interim President Delcy Rodriguez defended the response, stating that thousands of troops and officials were dispatched to the affected areas.
Recovery efforts continue as workers use heavy machinery to clear collapsed structures while families still search for the bodies of their loved ones.
caption:
Nearly 3,000 dead and 50,000 missing after twin earthquakes strike Venezuela.

Venezuela's devastating twin earthquakes, consisting of 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude shocks that occurred just 38 seconds apart, have killed 2,954 people according to official figures.

The disaster hit hardest in the coastal La Guaira area north of the capital Caracas, where numerous residential complexes were flattened and the Maiquetia international airport was damaged.

The United Nations estimates that as many as 50,000 people remain unaccounted for, while over 16,000 others have been injured.

International rescue teams, including squads from the US and South America, are now winding down search operations as the critical 72-hour window for survivors has passed.

The UN also estimates that the earthquakes caused $6.7 billion in physical damage, equivalent to approximately six percent of Venezuela's GDP.

Many Venezuelans have expressed anger over the government's slow response, claiming families had to dig out loved ones themselves before international aid arrived.

Interim President Delcy Rodriguez defended the response, stating that thousands of troops and officials were dispatched to the affected areas.

Recovery efforts continue as workers use heavy machinery to clear collapsed structures while families still search for the bodies of their loved ones.

headline: 103F heat and storms: Trump pushes ahead with US 250th birthday speech
summary: Despite record-breaking heat and severe thunderstorms that forced thousands to evacuate the National Mall, the US President insisted on delivering his address.
details: US President Donald Trump vowed to deliver his highly anticipated speech in Washington on Saturday to mark America's 250th birthday, regardless of severe weather conditions.

Tens of thousands of spectators were ordered to evacuate the National Mall several hours before the address due to approaching thunderstorms, leading to chaotic scenes as some attendees refused to leave.
Temperatures in the capital reached a record-breaking 103F (39.4C), the highest ever recorded for July 4th, as 160 million Americans faced extreme weather warnings.
Trump, 80, stated on Truth Social that storms bring luck and excitement, insisting he would be there 'no matter what,' even if it meant speaking at 2:00 AM.
A White House official and the Freedom 250 organizing group eventually rescheduled the address for 11 PM on Saturday night, followed by a fireworks show.

The celebrations were marked by political tension, with masked men carrying Confederate flags and white supremacist logos gathered near Capitol Hill, while Pope Leo XIV called for the welcoming of immigrants.
A Quinnipiac University Poll indicates that 61 percent of Americans believe the US is not living up to the ideals of the Declaration of Independence.
Inclement weather along the Eastern seaboard also disrupted celebrations in New York, Philadelphia, and Boston.
